teaser: Seven releases in one afternoon turned the reading meter into a working model: pay after you read, and the rating sets the price.
core_idea: On 10 October the reading meter became a working pay-on-demand publication in seven releases in 3 hours 40 minutes: pay for the share read from a balance that can go below zero, rate usefulness after reading to set the price from free to double, personas and newsrooms kept in the reader's browser, and consented, encrypted sharing for a designed front page. Paying after the value inverts Leanpub's pay-before model and is supported, with caveats, by pay-what-you-want evidence; Blendle's refunds show ratings measure quality. Each feature grew from using the last, which a Wardley map shows: new components on the left, built on commodities already there. It was fast because of non-functional work done before. Every decision started from not ripping off the reader. What is missing is traffic.

quotes.text: The only question left is whether people will pay for it.
If you saw the value, pay; if you saw more value, pay more; if you did not, do not.

quotes.text: The afternoon was cheap because the right-hand side of the map was already built.
